Fourteen methods call `trace::async_op` directly, all in the `tokio` crate. I found them by grepping for `async_op` and mapping each of the 14 call sites to the function that contains it. The function is `pub(crate)`, so no other crate in the workspace can call it.

I didn't use the index tool's answer. It returned callers of a different function, `async_trace_leaf`, and that list doesn't match this one.

- **`tokio/src/time/interval.rs`**: `Interval::tick`
- **`tokio/src/sync/mutex.rs`**: `Mutex::lock`, `Mutex::lock_owned`
- **`tokio/src/sync/rwlock.rs`**: `RwLock::read`, `RwLock::read_owned`, `RwLock::write`, `RwLock::write_owned`
- **`tokio/src/sync/barrier.rs`**: `Barrier::wait`
- **`tokio/src/sync/oneshot.rs`**: `Sender::closed`
- **`tokio/src/sync/semaphore.rs`**: `Semaphore::acquire`, `Semaphore::acquire_many`, `Semaphore::acquire_owned`, `Semaphore::acquire_many_owned`

Some files, such as `time/sleep.rs`, `sync/batch_semaphore.rs` and part of `oneshot.rs`, only use the `"runtime.resource.async_op"` span name. They don't call the function, so they aren't listed.
